fixes.root_cause: When active_flow='contact' (escalate_only mode), the LLM was still invoked for all utterances. The LLM mis-classified 'no that is wrong' as the 'escalate' intent. In escalate_only mode, only escalation intents are allowed to break out of the flow — so this misclassification caused an unintended agent transfer instead of routing back to the contact node for re-collection. The contact.py confirming step already handled 'no' correctly (lines 104-109), but the router never reached it.
fixes.fix_description:
Two changes applied:
(1) router.py: Added _is_confirmation_no() keyword function that detects negation/correction phrases ('that is wrong', 'that is incorrect', 'not right', 'no', 'wrong', 'nope', 'incorrect') when no escalation keywords are present. In escalate_only mode, if this check fires, the intent is forced back to the active flow BEFORE the LLM is called. This prevents the misclassification window entirely.
(2) contact.py confirming step: When the caller says 'no', the node now checks which specific field was being confirmed (address vs phone) and re-prompts for that specific field directly ('Please provide the new street address...') rather than returning to the top-level 'address or phone?' question. This saves one extra round-trip.
fixes.regression_risk: LOW-MEDIUM. _is_confirmation_no() only fires in escalate_only mode (contact, document, payment, policy, loan, beneficiary, privacy). The word-set {'no', 'nope', 'wrong', 'incorrect'} does not overlap with any VALID_INTENTS keywords. The escalation keyword guard inside _is_confirmation_no() ensures 'no I want a human agent' still escalates correctly. Existing PASS tests for contact flow (L1-011, L1-012, L1-013) should still pass. The contact.py confirming fallback path (both-fields-or-unclear) is preserved.
assumptions: The QA test 'no that is wrong' was spoken at the address confirmation prompt, meaning new_address was populated but new_phone was not. The targeted re-prompt logic handles this correctly.

'No thank you' was added to _GOODBYE_KEYWORDS (ISSUE-2-002) which could theoretically fire instead of _is_confirmation_no if spoken in a confirmation step. However the goodbye check runs before the escalate_only guard, so if a caller says 'no thank you' while in address confirmation they will be routed to goodbye. This is an edge case and the expected UX behavior — the caller is explicitly saying they want to leave.

fixes.root_cause: In router.py, the unauthenticated auth redirect (lines 100-101 original) ran before any goodbye check. Since 'goodbye' was not in _ESCALATION_KEYWORDS and _caller_wants_escalation() only checked escalation words, the keyword check at line 96 did not catch it. The LLM classification path was also blocked by the early auth redirect, so the LLM never ran to classify 'goodbye'. Additionally even if the LLM ran, lines 132-133 redirected any non-escalate intent to auth if not authenticated. There was no path for goodbye to bypass the auth wall.
fixes.fix_description: Added _caller_wants_goodbye() keyword function and _GOODBYE_KEYWORDS set in router.py. The goodbye check is placed at the very top of the decision tree — BEFORE the escalation check and BEFORE the auth wall redirect. If any goodbye keyword matches ('goodbye', 'bye', 'hang up', 'that is all', 'thank you goodbye', 'thanks goodbye', 'no thank you', 'no thanks'), the router immediately returns intent='goodbye' without touching auth state. This routes to goodbye_node which produces a farewell + Hangup TwiML response.
fixes.regression_risk: LOW. The goodbye check is keyword-only and runs before auth logic, so authenticated callers saying goodbye also route to goodbye_node (which is the correct existing behavior — L1-015 PASS). The only regression risk is if a caller says 'no thank you' (in _GOODBYE_KEYWORDS) during an active service flow while authenticated — they would be routed to goodbye. This is arguably correct UX. 'No thanks' / 'no thank you' are also in _is_confirmation_no's word set (via 'no') but the goodbye check runs first, so they take priority.
assumptions: Including 'no thank you' and 'no thanks' in _GOODBYE_KEYWORDS is intentional — these are common IVR closing phrases. If QA finds these cause false positives mid-flow, they can be removed from the set.
The goodbye_node does not require authentication state — confirmed by reading goodbye.py (routes to END with Hangup TwiML).

fixes.root_cause: The LLM ainvoke() call in router_node had no retry logic. A single Groq 503/429 error immediately propagated to the except block in twilio_voice.py, which performed a graceful escalation (transfer to agent). This is correct for permanent errors but wasteful for transient capacity errors that resolve in 1-2 seconds. Under concurrent load, multiple callers could all get agent-transferred simultaneously even though Groq recovers quickly.
fixes.fix_description: Added _invoke_llm_with_retry() async function in router.py. It wraps _llm.ainvoke() with up to 3 attempts. On 503/429/overloaded/capacity/rate limit errors, it waits 1s (attempt 1) or 2s (attempt 2) using asyncio.sleep before retrying. Non-retryable errors (network errors, auth errors, 4xx other than 429) still raise immediately. If all 3 attempts fail, the router falls back to the active_flow's mapped intent (stays in flow if mid-flow) or 'escalate' (if no active flow), rather than hard-crashing. Does not require tenacity — implemented with native asyncio. No new dependencies added.
fixes.regression_risk: LOW. The retry logic only activates on specific transient error strings. Normal successful calls are unaffected (no overhead). The fallback on total retry exhaustion ('escalate' or active_flow intent) matches the existing behavior from the original except block in twilio_voice.py. The asyncio.sleep calls are non-blocking — other concurrent callers' coroutines continue unaffected during the wait.
assumptions: Error strings from langchain-groq 1.1.3 contain '503', '429', 'overloaded', 'capacity', or 'rate limit' for the relevant transient errors. If the error format differs in future Groq SDK versions, the retry matching strings may need updating.
2^attempt delay (1s, 2s) was chosen to stay well under Twilio's 30-second TwiML timeout. Total worst-case retry time is ~3s which is acceptable for IVR.

fixes.root_cause: The privacy_node immediately read the GLBA opt-out script ('Under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, you have the right to limit the sharing...') with no preamble when first invoked. Callers who asked 'how do you use my personal information' received an opt-out menu with no actual answer to their question. For callers routed to escalation (as in L3-014), no disclosure was spoken at all before the transfer.
fixes.fix_description: Added PRIVACY_DISCLOSURE constant ('Our privacy policy governs how we use your personal information to service your policy and as required by law.') in privacy.py and prepended it to the GLBA_SCRIPT in the read_script step. Callers now hear the brief general disclosure before the opt-out options. Note: the L3-014 escalation behavior (LLM routing 'how do you use my information' directly to escalation rather than to privacy_node) was not changed — that is PASS-WITH-NOTE behavior. This fix only covers the case where privacy_node IS invoked.
fixes.regression_risk: NONE. The change only adds a prepended string to the TTS output on the initial step. All downstream logic (collecting_choice, confirming, _submit_opt_out) is unchanged. The 'read again' path (step confirming -> no -> read_script) now also benefits from the disclosure on the re-read.
assumptions: The brief disclosure text is an internal summary, not a verbatim regulatory script. If the legal/compliance team requires a specific verbatim disclosure, the PRIVACY_DISCLOSURE constant should be updated with their approved language.
The L3-014 PASS-WITH-NOTE status (router escalating general privacy questions rather than routing to privacy_node) is acceptable per QA notes and was not changed by this fix.
fixes.qa_clarification_note: QA should confirm whether the PRIVACY_DISCLOSURE text is legally sufficient or whether a verbatim approved disclosure script needs to be inserted. The current text is a functional placeholder.

new_fixes_2026_06_24.title: Auth fallback: caller says they don't know their phone/policy/DOB/name
new_fixes_2026_06_24.root_cause: No IDK (I-don't-know) guard existed in any auth step. Utterances like 'I don't know my phone number' were passed to normalize_phone_with_hint() which returned empty digits, falling into the generic retry loop and leaving the caller stuck.
new_fixes_2026_06_24.fix_description:
Created utils/idk_detector.py with is_idk(text) function. Applied to all 6 auth steps:
  collecting_phone  → IDK → collecting_policy ('No problem. <policy prompt>')
  confirming_phone  → IDK → collecting_policy
  collecting_policy → IDK → _escalate()
  collecting_dob    → IDK → collecting_name ('No problem. <name prompt>')
  confirming_dob    → IDK → collecting_dob re-ask ('No problem, please say the date of birth again')
  collecting_name   → IDK → _escalate() (last fallback)
new_fixes_2026_06_24.regression_risk: LOW — IDK check fires only when the utterance contains known uncertainty phrases. Real PII values (phone numbers, policy numbers, dates, names) do not contain IDK phrases. Verified by unit test: 17/17 cases correct, zero false positives.

new_fixes_2026_06_24.title: IDK handling in all ask steps across contact, document, and otp nodes
new_fixes_2026_06_24.root_cause: Same root cause — no IDK handling in any service node. Callers saying 'I don't know' at any question prompt triggered a parse failure and confusing re-prompt.
new_fixes_2026_06_24.fix_description:
Applied is_idk() guard to all ask steps:

contact_node:
  collecting (what to change?)  → IDK → graceful exit, offer rep
  collecting_address            → IDK → graceful exit, offer rep
  collecting_phone              → IDK → graceful exit, offer rep
  confirming                    → IDK → falls through to existing no-branch (re-collect field)

document_node:
  collecting_type  → IDK → graceful exit, offer rep
  ask_delivery     → IDK → graceful exit, offer rep

otp_node:
  choosing_method  → IDK → graceful exit, offer rep (active_flow='')

faq_node: skipped — RAG+LLM handles vague utterances naturally.
payment/loan/beneficiary nodes: skipped — informational only, no ask steps.
new_fixes_2026_06_24.regression_risk: LOW — All IDK guards inserted before the field's parse/detect call. Callers who know their address, phone, or document type are unaffected.
